analysis.title: GS Global Equities Call - 13 Nov 2026
key_insights: US futures up small pre-market: SPX +25bps, NDX +15bps, RTY +25bps, UST 10yr -2.5bps at 4.85%, WTI -10bps at $88.65. Overnight news light apart from the global MSFT 365 outage (MSFT -1.5% pre-market).
NVDA recovering (+2% pre-market). AMAT (+60bps pre-market), CBRS (+17%) and CSCO (-2.75%) reported solid earnings last night, with CBRS the outperformer.

Calendar today: US PPI, Eurozone GDP, NY Fed-ECB conference on nonbank financial institutions. Fed speakers: Collins (non-voter, 9:10 AM), Bowman (voter, 10:50 AM), Daly (non-voter, 12 PM), Jefferson (voter, 7 PM). RVTY investor day.
Next week: Warsh speaks Monday 11/16, NVDA reports 11/17, retail earnings (HD 11/17, LOW/TGT 11/18, WMT 11/19), China tech earnings (Tencent 11/18, BABA 11/19), Trump meets Xi 11/18-11/19.

GS Macro Outlook 2027: global growth was 2.7% in 2026 and is forecast at 2.8% in 2027. Strong AI capex, easier financial conditions and fiscal expansion offset the energy supply shock in 2026. In 2027, lower energy prices and AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.

Macro risks are tilted to the downside: renewed Iran escalation could cause another energy price surge, large fiscal deficits could push long-term yields up more sharply (especially France), and AI capex could disappoint from capacity constraints, regulation, credit stress or weaker demand.

Inflation should slow in 2027 after 2026 upside surprises: US tariff pass-through is ending, the energy impulse fades as the Iran war outbreak is lapped, and AI-related pressures ease as production capacity rises.

GS expects two more Fed hikes and one ECB hike, then a return to cuts in late 2027. Most other central bank forecasts are below market pricing, so GS expects longer-term rates to fall modestly despite large deficits and heavy AI-linked borrowing.

GS expects positive returns for equities and bonds in 2027 but a bumpy path. The AI boom has affected earnings and market values far more than GDP growth, and markets may question whether the record share of GDP going to US earnings can persist as the capex impulse peaks.

Oil price spike risk supports commodities as a hedge. Real yields are the highest in many years, so bonds are regaining hedging value. Equity index volatility is more likely to rise than fall, and GS sees longer-dated options as useful portfolio protection.
Chart titles note that markets have stopped rewarding higher AI capex and upward revisions have slowed.

GS 2027 equity outlook ('Finding Value in Growth'): 2026 returns were broad-based across regions and driven by earnings growth, with valuations moderating. Earnings growth is on course to slow sharply across all major regions in 2027, AI capex growth is likely to peak, and the cost of capital stays elevated.
Equities have de-rated sharply. With better valuations, slower but positive growth, and lower yields, inflation and oil, GS expects equities to keep rising with high volatility.

GS favors Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower yields, with long-duration Growth, particularly US Hyperscalers, highlighted. Regional stance: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe. Forecast returns are highest in Asia but GS prioritizes risk-adjusted returns.

Momentum regime shift: 12m Momentum (GSPRHIMO) had its best outperformance day in GS records yesterday versus 3m and 6m Momentum. Correlation between 12m and 3m momentum is now negative as the AI trade has unwound. AI names in the short legs of 3m and 6m momentum have surged while those in the long legs have fallen.
Info tech was net sold in 3m and 6m momentum but slightly bought in 12m momentum. 12m momentum will be a net seller of semis and buyer of software.

Prime book momentum exposure fell sharply from its 2026 peak to the 23rd percentile of its 5-year range. Data Center basket crowding is at the 1st percentile over 6 months. GS flags tactical shorts in former 12m momentum short names, or broadening into lower-quality software and staples, if the rotation resumes.
Chart of the day: rates are back in focus as the market reprices after this week's CPI print. A US 10yr +2 sigma move equals 5.25%, the level where GS asks when equities start to care.
Linked GS content describes two consecutive months of hot CPI, with GS EM Marketstrats arguing the Fed is behind the curve.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong AI capex has driven earnings and market values, and still-strong capex plus lower energy prices support 2.8% global growth in 2027 and continued equity gains.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex growth peaks in 2027, markets have stopped rewarding higher capex, and capex could disappoint from capacity constraints, regulation, credit stress or weaker demand. Markets may question the record share of GDP going to US earnings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI capex disappointing from capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress or weaker demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower bond yields, inflation and oil prices in 2027 support equity gains, and longer-term rates should come down modestly.
tension_points.bear_case: Hot CPI prints are repricing rates and a US 10yr move to +2 sigma (5.25%) is where equities may start to care. Large deficits could push long-term yields up sharply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US 10yr yield reaching 5.25%, a +2 sigma move.
